negative_snippets:
I stayed here for two days, and the overall experience was just average. The management and staff need to learn a bit of humility & social skills.

From check-in to check-out, their behavior was consistently cold and unwelcoming.

The in-house food is unreasonably expensive, and outside food is not allowed whenever their kitchen is open. This is something you should be aware of in advance. Even if you raise concerns, they may accommodate you once or twice, but the same behavior continues.

The rooms are decent, slightly above average but there is nothing particularly impressive. They are clean and tidy, as expected. The amenities are basic, similar to what you find in most places. The rooms are also quite small and lack proper ventilation. I had to keep the balcony door open for airflow, which can be uncomfortable at night for some people.
Regardless of the room category you choose, the management seriously needs to train their staff on proper guest interaction and behavior.

The only food thing was Good Quality food but then it's unreasonably expensive. The staff at the reception needs to be trained.

Only stay here if you want to get food poisoning by eating food from their in-house restaurant -
The hotel forcefully restricted us from ordering food from outside and insisted that we eat only from their in-house restaurant. This was not communicated clearly at the time of booking and felt very unreasonable and uncomfortable. Guests should have the freedom to choose their food, especially when staying for such a short duration.

Unfortunately, the food we were forced to eat caused serious health issues. We ordered simple items like pakoda and dal chawal, but the oil used was clearly stale or of very poor quality. That same night and the following day, both my husband and I suffered badly. My husband got a severe food infection, and I experienced intense stomach pain, nausea, and a horrible after-taste that lasted for days.

It has now been three days, and I am still dealing with stomach discomfort and weakness. This kind of experience is unacceptable from a hotel, especially when guests are not even allowed alternatives. Food safety and guest well-being should be a priority, not forced dependency.
I stayed at this hotel in Gurgaon for one day with my husband. At first, everything seemed fine — the room was decent, and the staff appeared polite. However, our overall experience turned extremely unpleasant because of one very serious issue that I feel people should know about before booking.

Because of this extremely unpleasant and unhealthy experience, I do not feel comfortable returning to this hotel and would strongly advise management to reconsider such policies and improve food quality. This was truly disappointing and distressing.
